title.en: Who did it, and why hide them?
title.es: ¿Quién lo hizo y por qué omitirlo?

es: Explicar por qué un texto informativo omite al agente (desconocido, obvio o irrelevante) y cuándo conviene mantenerlo.

teaching.en: The statue was stolen in 1998, and the thief has never been found.
teaching.es: La estatua fue robada en 1998 y el ladrón nunca ha sido encontrado.
teaching.explanationEs: Agente desconocido: la guía no puede decir quién fue, así que omite el agente.
segments: The statue was stolen in 1998, and
the thief has never been found.
teaching.audioText: The statue was stolen in 1998, and the thief has never been found.

teaching.en: The suspect was arrested last week.
teaching.es: El sospechoso fue arrestado la semana pasada.
teaching.explanationEs: Agente obvio: la policía. Repetirlo sería redundante.
teaching.audioText: The suspect was arrested last week.

teaching.en: «Mistakes were made» can conceal who is responsible.
teaching.es: «Se cometieron errores» puede ocultar quién es el responsable.
teaching.explanationEs: La pasiva sin agente también puede esconder a quien tiene la culpa.
teaching.audioText: «Mistakes were made» can conceal who is responsible.

teaching.en: The mayor was blamed for the flood, but nobody knows who is to blame.
teaching.es: Culparon al alcalde de la inundación, pero nadie sabe quién tiene la culpa.
teaching.explanationEs: Was blamed es pasiva; to blame es una expresión fija: tener la culpa.
segments: The mayor was blamed for the flood,
but nobody knows who is to blame.
teaching.audioText: The mayor was blamed for the flood, but nobody knows who is to blame.

teaching.en: It is unclear who opened the gate, so the guide says only that it was opened at night.
teaching.es: No está claro quién abrió la puerta, así que la guía solo dice que se abrió de noche.
teaching.explanationEs: Si no se sabe el agente, la pasiva permite informar igualmente.
segments: It is unclear who opened the gate, so the
guide says only that it was opened at night.
teaching.audioText: It is unclear who opened the gate, so the guide says only that it was opened at night.

teaching.en: The gate is locked every night; who locks it is irrelevant for visitors.
teaching.es: La puerta se cierra con llave cada noche; quién la cierra es irrelevante para los visitantes.
teaching.explanationEs: Agente irrelevante: al visitante solo le importa el dato.
segments: The gate is locked every night; who
locks it is irrelevant for visitors.
teaching.audioText: The gate is locked every night; who locks it is irrelevant for visitors.

prompt.es: ¿Por qué se omite el agente en esta frase?

choices.text: Because the agent is obvious.
Because the agent is very famous.
Because we do not know who did it.

feedback.es: No se sabe quién robó la estatua, por eso la guía no puede nombrar al agente.

prompt.es: ¿Por qué aquí se mantiene el agente?

choices.text: Because the name gives useful information.
Because the agent is unknown.
Because the agent is irrelevant.

feedback.es: El nombre del arquitecto es un dato valioso para el visitante, por eso se mantiene con by.

hint.es: ¿Aporta algo al visitante el nombre del arquitecto?

origin.text: The church was designed by Gaudí.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La puerta se cierra con llave todas las noches.»

answer.text: The gate is locked every night
accepted: The gate is locked every night
Every night the gate is locked

feedback.es: Presente pasivo: is + participio, sin by porque quién la cierra es irrelevante.

hint.es: Presente pasivo: be + participio, sin agente.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el motivo de omitir el agente.

pairs: The suspect was arrested last week.
Tickets are checked at the door.

feedback.es: Tres motivos distintos: obvio (la policía), desconocido (el ladrón) e irrelevante (quien cierra la puerta).

pairs: The suspect was arrested last week.
Tickets are checked at the door.

prompt.es: ¿Qué agente se mantiene en este fragmento?

choices.text: The people who damaged it.
The artist who made the statue.
The workers who repaired it.

feedback.es: Solo se nombra a la autora de la estatua, porque aporta información; quien la dañó y quien la reparó se omiten.

origin.text: The statue in the square was made by a famous artist, Ana Ruiz. It was damaged in 1970, and it was repaired in 2005.

prompt.es: Escribe la versión de guía: nadie sabe quién rompió la ventana.

answer.text: The window was broken last night.
accepted: The window was broken last night.
The window got broken last night.
Last night the window was broken.
Last night the window got broken.

feedback.es: Se pasa el objeto a sujeto y se omite el agente desconocido: The window was broken.

origin.text: Someone broke the window last night.

prompt.es: ¿Qué hecho aparece sin agente porque se desconoce?

choices.text: The plans for the tower.
The repairs in 1955.
The damage in 1944.

feedback.es: El texto dice «nobody knows who did it» sobre el daño de 1944; los planos sí tienen agente y las reparaciones no lo necesitan.

origin.text: The clock tower was built in 1720. The plans were prepared by the architect Louis Pelletier. In 1944 the tower was damaged, but nobody knows who did it. It was repaired in 1955.

prompt.es: Escucha la guía y elige qué agente nombra y cuál omite.

choices.text: It names the architect but not who repaired the roof.
It names who repaired the roof but not the architect.
It names the person who opens the doors every morning.

feedback.es: La guía nombra a la arquitecta Elena Ruiz (dato informativo) y omite quién reparó el techo y quién abre las puertas.

origin.audio: Welcome to the old market. It was built in 1890 by a famous architect, Elena Ruiz. The roof was repaired last year, and the doors are opened every morning at eight.

prompt.es: ¿Qué efecto tiene la pasiva sin agente en la frase del alcalde?

choices.text: It proves that nobody made mistakes.
It avoids saying who is responsible.
It gives the exact date of the mistakes.

feedback.es: «Mistakes were made» no dice quién se equivocó: la omisión puede ocultar al responsable.

origin.text: The mayor says: «Mistakes were made in the project.»

prompt.es: Ordena: «La estatua fue robada y el ladrón nunca fue encontrado.»

answer.text: The statue was stolen and the thief was never found

feedback.es: Dos pasivas seguidas sin agente: no se sabe quién robó la estatua.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase mantiene el agente por ser informativo?

choices.text: The wall was painted by someone.
The wall was painted by people.
The wall was painted by the artist Ana Ruiz.

feedback.es: El nombre de la artista aporta información; someone y people no añaden nada y se omitirían.

prompt.es: Completa: «Quién cierra la puerta es irrelevante para los visitantes.»

feedback.es: Irrelevant indica que el dato no importa al lector, motivo para omitir al agente.

origin.text: Who locks the gate is ___ for visitors.

prompt.es: Reescribe sin el agente obvio: la policía arrestó al sospechoso el lunes.

answer.text: The suspect was arrested on Monday.
accepted: The suspect was arrested on Monday.
The suspect got arrested on Monday.

feedback.es: El agente (la policía) es obvio; se pasa el sospechoso a sujeto y se omite by the police.

origin.text: The police arrested the suspect on Monday.
